source: Yao et al. (2022) ReAct
finding: Interleaving a thought with each action (act, observe, re-think) beats acting with no thoughts. This is the emergent-strategy loop: no full plan, the next step follows the last observation.
numbers: ALFWorld: best ReAct trial 71% success, best Act 45%, BUTLER (imitation) 37%; worst ReAct trial 48%. ReAct beats Act in six trials, gain 33% to 90%, mean 62%. 134 unseen games. WebShop: IL+RL 28.7% SR (table 4).
limits: Few-shot prompts, PaLM-540B, two text environments. Without thoughts the agent loses track of state and fails to decompose goals.
agent_relevance: Per-step reasoning from fresh observation is a strong default; S9-style learning from action needs a visible thought each step.

source: Yao et al. (2022) ReAct error analysis (HotpotQA)
finding: Chain-of-thought alone (pure up-front reasoning, no feedback) hallucinates; ReAct has fewer hallucinations but more reasoning loops.
numbers: Error table: reasoning error (wrong trace, repeated steps) 47% of ReAct failures vs 16% of CoT failures. Abstract: ReAct overcomes hallucination and error propagation of CoT.
quote: Wrong reasoning trace (including failing to recover from repetitive steps)
limits: Failure analysis on a small manual sample; Wikipedia API only.
agent_relevance: Pure planning in the head drifts; pure reactive loops repeat. Need loop detector (code-checked) plus grounding.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion
finding: After a failed trial the agent writes a verbal lesson, stored in memory, and retries. This is learning from realized outcomes (the S9 loop).
numbers: ALFWorld: ReAct+Reflexion solved 130 of 134 tasks in 12 trials; ReAct-only plateaus between trials 6 and 7. Gain 22% absolute on ALFWorld, 20% HotPotQA, 11% HumanEval; HumanEval pass@1 91% vs GPT-4 80%.
quote: ReAct + Reflexion significantly outperforms ReAct by completing 130 out of 134 tasks
limits: Memory is a sliding window; can stick in local minima; needs a clean success/fail signal and a heuristic to detect hallucinated state.
agent_relevance: Matches G2: revise from real failing output. Lessons need a code-checked signal, not self-opinion.

source: Shinn et al. (2023) Reflexion failure pattern
finding: Common baseline failure: agent thinks it holds an item it does not, and repeats actions. Reflexion triggers on such repetition or hallucination.
numbers: Hallucination rate converges at 22% in the no-memory baseline with no recovery (figure text).
limits: Single environment family.
agent_relevance: Supports a deterministic loop/hallucination trigger rather than scheduled doubt (G1).

source: Wang et al. (2025) Plan-and-Act
finding: A planner writes the high-level plan, an executor does it. Making the plan revisable (dynamic replanning) gave a large gain over a static plan.
numbers: WebArena-Lite ablation: no planner 36.97; base planner 17.16-23.63; synthetic data 30.30; plan expansion 39.40; targeted augmentation 43.63; fine-tuned static 43.63-53.94; dynamic replanning +10.31 over static planner, to 53.94 (beating WebRL-3.1-70B at 49.1 by 4.84); with CoT 57.58. Full WebArena: 45.7 (Llama-70B), 48.15 (QwQ-32B). Zero-shot GPT-4-Turbo 17.6, GPT-4o 13.9 as executors in prior rows.
limits: Planner and executor are fine-tuned on synthetic data; benefit depends on training the replanner.
agent_relevance: Direct evidence that plan plus revision from observation beats either alone: deliberate and emergent combined.

source: Wang et al. (2025) Plan-and-Act base executor result
finding: Even an untrained executor jumps when given a good dynamic plan: the plan carries the reasoning, the executor only grounds it.
numbers: Base executor with plan: 44.24% vs 9.85% with no planner (+34.39 points) on WebArena-Lite.
limits: Plan quality came from a finetuned planner.
agent_relevance: Split the work: model plans in chunks, code tracks which plan step is live.

source: Prasad et al. (2023) ADaPT as-needed decomposition
finding: Plan only when the executor fails: try the task directly, decompose recursively on failure. Beats both upfront static decomposition and pure reactive execution.
numbers: ALFWorld all-tasks, table 1 (dmax=3): ReAct 43.3, Plan-and-Execute 43.3, Try Again 47.8, Reflexion 57.5, ADaPT 71.6. Appendix table (probably another LLM): ReAct 56.7, P&E 63.4, Reflexion 67.2, ADaPT 79.8. Abstract: up to +28.3% ALFWorld, +27% WebShop, +33% TextCraft.
limits: Which LLM belongs to which table was not clear from extracted text; TextCraft is the authors' own dataset.
agent_relevance: Planning triggered by a failure signal fits G1: replan only on check failure, not on schedule.

source: Prasad et al. (2023) ADaPT WebShop and TextCraft
finding: Static decomposition up front can be worse than no plan on WebShop: committing early hurts when the plan is wrong. On TextCraft plan-and-execute beat ReAct.
numbers: WebShop SR: iterative executor-only 29.0, static decomposition 17.0, retry 30.0, Reflexion 35.0, LATS 38.0 (ReAct 32.0, Plan-and-Execute 17.0 in table 1). TextCraft: ReAct 19, Plan-and-Execute 27, Reflexion 32. TextCraft depth-2 recipes 26.9% to 78.2%, depth 3 1.8% to 38.7% with ADaPT.
limits: Mixed result: task structure decides which side wins.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition: planning wins on compositional tasks with known structure, loses where the environment surprises.

source: Prasad et al. (2023) ADaPT cross-model planning
finding: A plan from one model can help a different, smaller executor model.
numbers: Improves success by up to 19.9% over executor-only (ReAct); gains not simply from more LLM calls.
limits: Table text partly garbled in extraction.
agent_relevance: Cheap planner / separate executor is a viable split.

source: Valmeekam et al. (2022) PlanBench
finding: Models are weak at generating plans from scratch, better at replanning and reuse, best at goal reformulation.
numbers: Blocksworld 600 instances: GPT-4 plan generation 206/600 (34.3%), InstructGPT-3 6.8%. Mystery Blocksworld deceptive 26/600 (4.3%), randomized 12/600 (2%). GPT-4 replanning 48.1%, plan reuse 65.3%, plan verification 58.6%, goal reformulation 76.8-87%.
limits: Classical toy domain, early models; later reasoning models do better (not measured here).
agent_relevance: Forming a plan from scratch is the weak step, so revising after seeing results is the easier lever.

source: Kambhampati et al. (2024) LLMs Can't Plan, But Can Help Planning in LLM-Modulo Frameworks
finding: Position: autoregressive LLMs cannot plan or self-verify alone; pair them with external model-based verifiers in a loop.
numbers: No benchmark numbers (position paper).
limits: Conceptual, not empirical.
agent_relevance: Same as G2/G5: code verifies, model proposes.

source: Xie et al. (2024) TravelPlanner
finding: Long-horizon planning with many constraints is hard for agents; they fail to track several constraints at once.
numbers: GPT-4 success rate 0.6% (abstract).
limits: Single benchmark; later models improved.
agent_relevance: Upfront plans break on constraint tracking; use code to hold constraints.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Plan-and-Solve prompting
finding: Asking for a plan first, then solving, improves zero-shot chain-of-thought.
numbers: Over 10 datasets with GPT-3, Plan-and-Solve beats zero-shot CoT by a large margin; comparable to 8-shot CoT on math (abstract; exact figures not read).
limits: Abstract only; no exact numbers verified.
agent_relevance: A plan-first prompt is cheap; measured on reasoning, not open-world action.

source: Xu et al. (2023) ReWOO
finding: Plan all tool calls up front without seeing observations. Cheaper than ReAct and slightly more accurate on HotpotQA.
numbers: 5x token efficiency and 4% accuracy gain on HotpotQA (abstract).
limits: Baseline not named in the abstract; a static plan suits tasks whose steps do not depend on results.
agent_relevance: Boundary: a fully planned tool sequence works when steps are independent of earlier observations.

source: Sun et al. (2023) AdaPlanner
finding: A closed-loop planner refines its plan from environment feedback; contrasted with greedy or static plans.
numbers: Beats SOTA by 3.73% on ALFWorld and 4.11% on MiniWoB++; 2x fewer samples on ALFWorld, 600x fewer on MiniWoB++ (abstract).
limits: Abstract only; exact closed vs open loop numbers not read.
agent_relevance: Operationalizes intended-plus-realized strategy: replan from feedback.

source: Wang et al. (2023) Voyager
finding: Open-ended agent with automatic curriculum, skill library and iterative prompting from environment feedback. Behaviour emerges and is stored as reusable code.
numbers: 3.3x more unique items, 2.3x longer distances, tech-tree milestones up to 15.3x faster than prior SOTA.
limits: Minecraft only; GPT-4 as black box.
agent_relevance: Closest agent analogue of emergent patterns being consolidated into a library (S9).

source: Backlund and Petersson (2025) Vending-Bench
finding: Long-horizon business run (vending machine, 20M+ tokens per run): high variance, runs derail even for the best model.
numbers: Mean net worth over 5 runs: Claude 3.5 Sonnet $2,217.93; o3-mini $906.86; human (1 run) $844.05; Gemini 1.5 Pro $594.02; GPT-4o mini $582.33; GPT-4o $335.46. Days until sales stop: Sonnet 102, o3-mini 86, human 67. Correlation of failure with memory-full day r=0.167.
limits: 5 runs per model, 1 human run. Failures not tied to context filling.
agent_relevance: Coherence over time fails from misread state, so persistent verified state is needed.

source: Backlund and Petersson (2025) Vending-Bench failure cases
finding: Derailments: model assumed order arrived on the stated date; believed a 10-day sales drought meant failure; stopped calling tools for about 1,300 messages (o3-mini); thought it was out of money with half left (Gemini 1.5 Pro).
numbers: Sonnet shortest run about 18 days. Some runs recover (Gemini 2.0 Flash resumed sales after derailing).
limits: Anecdotes from a handful of runs.
agent_relevance: Supports a code-held ledger and a meltdown-loop detector.

source: Anthropic and Andon Labs (2025) Project Vend
finding: Claude Sonnet 3.7 ran an office shop for about a month and lost money: sold metal cubes below cost, gave discounts under pressure, invented a payment account. Authors expect better prompting, structured reflection on business results, search tools and a CRM to fix most failures.
numbers: About one month, one deployment. No exact net figure given; main loss came from metal-cube purchases.
limits: Single case; no controlled comparison; later upgrades reported as more reliable without numbers.
agent_relevance: An agent without a plan or ledger behaves opportunistically and inconsistently. Structured reflection on results is the authors' own fix.

source: AI and Strategic Decision-Making: Entrepreneurs and Investors (2024), Study 1
finding: GPT-3.5 rewrites of startup plans were rated slightly higher by 250 US investors (2,500 evaluations).
numbers: LLM plans +0.14 SD (p<0.001); accept recommendation +5 points (entrepreneur mean 57%, p=0.003); interest in intro +3 points (51%, p=0.094); investment likelihood +2.55 on 0-100 (46.69 base, p=0.007). For rejected plans gains +7, +8, +6 points; gains vanished for accepted plans. 10 plans (5 accepted, 5 rejected) from 309.
limits: 10 plans only, GPT-3.5, ratings not outcomes; authors call results conjectures.
agent_relevance: LLMs produce analysis-style plans that look credible; nothing here on whether a plan survives contact with action.

source: AI and Strategic Decision-Making: Entrepreneurs and Investors (2024), Study 2
finding: LLM scores of business plans track investor scores moderately.
numbers: 138 text-only plans of 731 (19%); 541 human evaluations by 137 judges, 3-5 per plan; LLM-investor correlation 0.52, R2 0.29; ICC 0.51 (AI vs VC averages) vs 0.25 between single VCs (significant only at 10%); KS p=0.86; 3 LLM scoring iterations averaged.
limits: Only text-only plans; scores correlate, no firm-performance link.
agent_relevance: A model rates an intended plan about as consistently as individual investors; predicting realized emergence is untested.

source: Lechner et al. (2024) Can GenAI do your next strategy task? Not yet (CMR Berkeley)
finding: Three case tests of GPT-4: market research dossier worked; consulting case framing was MECE but not hypothesis-driven; due diligence DCF failed.
numbers: Due diligence price per share: $28 first attempt, $96 on retry, correct about $35. Case interview parts 3-4 passing, framing below pass. o1-preview addendum: matched a top candidate on 4 of 5 case questions and 3 of 5 due-diligence tasks; same final share-price answer on resubmission while GPT-4 gave two very different answers.
limits: Single case studies, stochastic outputs; the 90% time saving is the authors' projection.
agent_relevance: Planning-as-analysis is where models are already competent; the synthesis step and arithmetic need checks and repeat runs.

source: Strategic management analysis: from data to strategy diagram by LLM (2024)
finding: LLMs can build most standard strategy-framework analyses (extract insights, organize under a framework, draw the diagram).
numbers: No quantitative evaluation reported; 7-page workshop paper (NLVIZ, IEEE VIZ 2024).
limits: No metrics at all.
agent_relevance: Shows the planning-as-analysis half is mechanizable, but unevaluated.

source: Search summary: How Well Can AI Do Strategy? (Strategy Science, 2026)
finding: Search summary says LLMs were benchmarked on the Back Bay Battery strategy simulation and struggled with strategic uncertainty.
numbers: No numbers seen. Page returned 403.
limits: Not opened; claim comes from a search summary only.
agent_relevance: Candidate for a follow-up read; do not rely on it.

source: Search summary: trendslop study on LLM strategic advice (2026)
finding: A secondary blog summary says LLMs favour trendy managerial options over fitting ones across binary strategic tensions.
numbers: No numbers seen. Page returned 404.
limits: Not opened; original paper unidentified.
agent_relevance: Possible bias to test: a planner that prefers fashionable strategy. Unverified.

source: Gap note: no LLM study found that tests the deliberate versus emergent distinction directly
finding: arXiv web search for LLM and strategic management returned 3 results, none on planned versus emergent strategy (2505.18779, 2501.10685, 2409.06643). OpenAlex, Semantic Scholar and arXiv APIs were rate limited; WebSearch budget was exhausted after one query.
numbers: 3 results on arXiv search; coverage limited by quota.
limits: Absence is weak evidence: the search was shallow.
agent_relevance: In agent work the contrast appears only as plan-then-act vs ReAct vs replanning; the mapping to Mintzberg is ours, not the authors'.

source: Cross-paper pattern: static plan vs revisable plan vs reactive loop
finding: Static upfront plans win where steps are independent and the world is stable (ReWOO, TextCraft). Revisable plans beat static ones where observations matter (Plan-and-Act +10.31; WebShop static decomposition 17 vs executor-only 29).
numbers: See ADaPT WebShop and Plan-and-Act lines.
limits: Cross-paper comparison; different models, benchmarks and training; our synthesis.
agent_relevance: Design rule: plan, but trigger replanning by a failed check, not by schedule.
